key_insight: A normal form for Pauli-based computation fully characterizes its adaptivity and entanglement, revealing a time-reversed relationship with one-way quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: The normal form supports ahead-of-time compilation that can reduce entangling-gate overhead and quantum memory requirements.
method: Express Pauli-based computation in a normal form exposing adaptive and entanglement structure.
Use this structure to guide distributed computation and analyze magic-state injection rates.
Detect and remove unnecessary magic-state qubits efficiently.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average reductions of 50% in CNOT gate count and 40% in quantum memory for random quantum circuits, outperforming other state-of-the-art compilers, plus an exponential improvement in detecting unnecessary magic-state qubits.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify benchmark sizes or hardware constraints, so practical gains on specific devices and workloads remain uncertain.
paper_title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
